problem: Find the equation of the right-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(1,-3)$ and passes through the point $(3,0).$

feedback.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068340/assets/1f6330a6e9bc0e48326982c7b7509f3e2257de994c5736c813ede93a07491e70.png)

What is the equation of the parabola shown above?
feedback.worked_solution:
From the diagram we see that the arms of the parabola open to the right. The parabola has its vertex at $(0,-3)$ and passes through the point $(3,0).$

The general standard equation of a parabola whose vertex is $(h,k)$ and whose arms open right or left is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-k)^{2} & =4p(x-h).\end{aligned}
$$

Since we know that the given parabola has its vertex at $(h,k)=(0,-3),$ we substitute $h=0$ and $k=-3$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+3)^{2} & =4px.\end{aligned}
$$

We also know that the given parabola passes through the point $(3,0),$ so we can substitute $x=3$ and $y=0$ into the equation above and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+3)^{2} & =4px \\ (0+3)^{2} & =4p(3) \\ 9 & =12p \\ p & =\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+3)^{2} & =4px \\ (y+3)^{2} & =4(\frac{3}{4})x \\ (y+3)^{2} & =3x.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the arms of the parabola open to the right since $p=\frac{3}{4}$ is positive.
